texts: Forty-three Keepers are active in the present generation.
Old Vesh is an old Keeper.
Old Vesh has retired from station-tending.

fields.sentence: Forty-three Keepers are active in the present generation.

q2_gaps: a framing/domain PP restricting a claim whose copular predicate must distribute over a group ('active in the present generation') — the instruction set anchors such a PP on 'what is claimed', but a distributed copular has no claim symbol, so no attachment site (group witness / per-member reified state / inside the rule's conclusion) is specified
review.notes: Counted plural takes the group + Cardinality 43, and the copular predicate distributes as (Implication (PartOf $x g) (Member $x active)) rather than riding the group symbol, both per doctrine; "present generation" is correctly left unfused as a descriptive modifier. Attaching the PP to the group with the preposition-named In (rather than LocatedIn, which a generation is not) is a defensible pick among the unspecified options.

(Inheritance keeper (can keep)) fires under the fixed copular-predicate licence for agent-nominalizations (strip -er leaves the standing verb 'keep'), at the specified definitional TV. 'young Keeper' correctly stays unfused as incidental description rather than a role title, and capitalized 'Keeper' in a predicate nominal is an ordinary lowercase kind.

q1_issues.issue: (Ordinal pell 2 year) mis-slots the attributive 'second-year' as Pell's RANK on a 'year' ordering, but Ordinal's scale slot is an associated event or an explicit '-est' dimension, and the sentence ranks Pell against nothing.
The attributive compound 'second-year Keeper' is not routed through Compound concepts, so the kind atom carries only 'keeper' and the stated restriction is carried by no licensed atom.

q2_gaps: numeral+noun attributive of tenure/stage ('a second-year Keeper', 'a third-year student') — Compound concepts assumes a single-word modifier and decomposes once to single-word lemmas, and nothing encodes 'is in one's Nth year of a role'
review.notes: Name symbol, Name atom and the lowercased 'keeper' lemma for the capitalized common noun are all correct; the defect is confined to how the 'second-year' modifier is carried.

issues.reason: Ordinal records an entity's rank n on an ordering scale (the associated event, or an explicit -est dimension), and this sentence ranks Pell against nothing, so (Ordinal pell 2 year) asserts a second position in some year-ordering that the text never states.

Core patterns bars silently dropping a stated restriction, and 'second-year Keeper' is a classifier plus role head of exactly the lifetime_member / senior_contractor type, so Compound concepts licenses a fused symbol with its head genus - the parse instead leaves the restriction carried by no licensed atom.

gaps_confirmed: A numeral-plus-noun tenure attributive ('a second-year Keeper', 'a third-year student'): Compound concepts decomposes once to single-word lemmas and so cannot unpack the multi-word modifier, and nothing encodes the underlying content 'is in one's Nth year of a role'. The fused symbol does carry the surface restriction opaquely, so the gap is in the internal analysis, not in the existence of a compliant form.
adjudication.defect_summary: Drop (Ordinal pell 2 year) entirely - nothing in the sentence ranks Pell - and carry the restriction through the compound: (Member pell second_year_keeper) with (Inheritance second_year_keeper keeper) (STV 1.0 0.99), no modifier genus, since 'second-year' fails the predication test exactly as 'assistant secretary' does; membership in keeper then derives from the genus rather than being separately asserted.
adjudication.notes: The name symbol, the single Name atom, and lowercasing the capitalized common noun to the class lemma keeper are all correct; the defect is confined to how the 'second-year' modifier is carried.

fields.sentence: Old Vesh is an old Keeper.

review.notes: Capitalized 'Old' correctly joins the name run (the 'Upper Calderwick' rule: one symbol, one Name, no separate (Member old_vesh upper)-style atom), while the predicate adjective 'old' is a separate Member atom rather than a fused compound, as incidental description requires. (Inheritance keeper (can keep)) fires on the copular-predicate trigger as written, though the instruction set's example for that trigger has a KIND subject ('Penguins are swimmers') and this clause has an individual one.

fields.sentence: Old Vesh has retired from station-tending.

q2_gaps: object-incorporating gerund/deverbal compound nominal used as a referring argument ("retired from station-tending") — the compound-action pattern is defined as verb_object and scoped to reified (can …)/(obligated …)/(permitted …) terms, so neither the symbol order for a surface object-first form (station_tend vs tend_station) nor the licence for a bare (Patient <compound> <object>) atom outside those terms is addressed

an abstract "from"-phrase naming an occupation or activity ceased ("retired from station-tending") — whether it answers "whence" and so takes the Source role, or takes the preposition-named From oblique, is not addressed
review.notes: The capitalized-run name handling (one opaque symbol old_vesh, one Name atom, no invented person type) and the perfect → (Past e) with no ordering atom (no other event to order against) both follow the instruction set. "Retired" is not one of the cessation wordings, so the absence of a strength-0 denial is correct.

q1_issues.issue: The Name string drops 'Old' even though the name is defined as exactly its capitalized run of words, which here is 'Old Vesh' (symbol old_vesh, one Name fact carrying the full surface form).

(Member vesh old) turns the capitalized premodifier into structure, which the mechanical casing rule bars for a capitalized modifier joining a name ('Upper Calderwick' gets no (Member ... upper)) and which the courtesy/kinship-title route would likewise keep as surface inside the Name string.

q2_gaps: A SENTENCE-INITIAL capitalized modifier before a proper noun ('Old Vesh attends ...'): the name rule decides name-hood 'by the casing itself, mechanically', but sentence-initial capitalization is orthographic and cannot distinguish a name-joining modifier from an ordinary predicative adjective, and no rule exempts that position.

A DETERMINERLESS capitalized institutional noun as a direct object ('attends Council'): the capitalized-common-noun-label rule presumes a definite ('the Assembly' -> 'definite handling as usual'), while the bare-class-symbol licence is reserved for non-specific / generic objects and forbidden for a specific definite individual, so a bare institutional 'Council' falls between the two.
review.notes: Everything else is right: Agent for the transitive subject, Theme for an unchanged direct object, no status atom on the present habitual, and correctly no Name atom for 'Council'.

issues.reason: Names and casing fixes a name as 'exactly its capitalized run of words', which here is 'Old Vesh', and the courtesy/kinship-title route likewise 'keep[s] the full form in the Name string' — so (Name vesh "Vesh") drops a surface word under every licensed route.

The mechanical casing rule states that a capitalized modifier joins the name and yields no modifier atom ('Upper Calderwick' is one symbol, 'no (Member … upper)'), so (Member vesh old) manufactures structure out of a name-internal word and asserts an age property the text only spells as part of the label.

gaps_confirmed: Sentence-initial capitalization defeats the 'decide by the casing itself, mechanically' cue: in that position a name-joining capitalized modifier and an ordinary adjective are orthographically identical, and no rule exempts or adjusts for it.

A determinerless capitalized institutional noun as a direct object ('attends Council') falls between the capitalized-common-noun-label rule (which presumes a definite — 'definite handling as usual') and the bare-class-symbol licence (reserved for non-specific / generic objects and barred for a specific definite individual).
new_gaps: An age / affection epithet premodifying a personal name ('Old Vesh') is claimed by two rules that disagree on the SYMBOL: the capitalized-run rule yields old_vesh, the courtesy/kinship-title rule yields vesh carrying the full string. Both keep 'Old' in the Name string, but nothing tie-breaks which symbol later mentions must reuse — and a wrong choice silently splits coreference.
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form keeps the whole capitalized run as one name — (Name old_vesh "Old Vesh"), every later mention on old_vesh — or, on the title reading, (Name vesh "Old Vesh"); either way exactly one Name fact carrying 'Old', and no (Member … old) atom at all.
adjudication.notes: The event half is right: Agent for the transitive subject, Theme for an unchanged direct object, and no status atom on the simple-present habitual.

q1_issues.issue: "apprentices" is the verb's sole direct object, which the role rules route to Patient/Theme by the does-it-change test, whereas Recipient is defined as the goal of a transfer surfacing as an indirect object or a "to"-phrase.

q2_gaps: a mono-transitive verb of teaching/communication whose only direct object is the addressee ("teaches apprentices", "told the crew") — the direct-object test yields Patient/Theme while the Recipient gloss covers addressees of communication, and nothing states which wins
review.notes: The name symbol/Name atom for the capitalized run "Old Vesh", the absence of any type atom for it, the absent status atom (bare simple present = habitual default) and the bare-kind object filler for a non-specific plural all follow the instruction set. The role head on the object is the only contested point.

issues.reason: Recipient's own gloss extends it to "the addressee of communication" on the ground that "a message is a transfer", and the apprentices are exactly that; the direct-object test does not settle a mono-transitive teach whose sole object is the ditransitive frame's first (indirect) object, so this is graceful improvisation in gap territory and (Recipient sk_teach_1 apprentice) is true of the sentence's content and well-typed.

gaps_confirmed: A mono-transitive verb of teaching/communication whose only object is the addressee ("teaches apprentices", "told the crew"): the direct-object test routes to Patient/Theme while Recipient's gloss covers addressees of communication, and nothing states which wins.
adjudication.notes: The rest conforms: "Old Vesh" as one opaque multi-word name symbol with no invented type atom and no modifier genus, Agent on the eventive teach, no status atom on the bare simple present habitual, and the bare kind filler for the non-specific plural object.
